body:
I would like to bring out the discussion about upgrading the built-in Hive support version from 1.2.1 to 2.3.x. The reason for this upgrading is:

The community is working on Hive Iceberg support, and there's some potential version problems (#170 (comment)).
The version 1.2.1 is quite old, most of the frameworks now move on to 2.3.x, like Spark.

Please share your comments.
CC @rdblue @rdsr .
title: Consider upgrading built-in Hive version to 2.3.x
Vectorized reads - explore replacing DateDayVector and TimestampMicroTZVector with IntVector and BigIntVector respectively
Vectorized reads- eagerly decode parquet dictionary encoded data for fixed width types

body: Currently, we are able to build multiple partition spec against a table through PartitionSpec Builder and commit through updatePartitionSpec from TableMetadata class. While we still don't have an explicit way to commit the partition evolution AFAIK.  I think we can create a UpdateParittionSpec interface and a Table API updateParitionSpec to do the job. What do you think?
title: Create a table API for partition evolution

body: As a side effect Iceberg can't determine that the file only contains matching data rows and can be deleted (when overwrite operation hits the same partition).
title: AvroFileAppender doesn't report column-level stats
Vectorized reads - enable vectorized reads when projecting identity partition columns
Unclosed input stream when reading manifestFile

title: IcebergGenerics should support ORC format
Add support for reading Avro and ORC data files in Iceberg Pig

body:
We are doing some work on support Mrv2 API. This API is will eventually be used by Pig and standalone MR.  There are other MR based frameworks which have not moved away from the older MRv1 api e.g Hive. Also AFAIK both apis are stable and neither has been marked deprecated.
We should provide support for Mrv1 API.  There are libraries which provide an automatic conversion from Mrv2 to Mrv1, e.g see #843 (comment), something to take inspiration from.
title: [Hive Support] Implement mapred Mrv1 API for Iceberg

body: We already have the Spark ORC writer written - org.apache.iceberg.spark.data.SparkOrcWriter . We need to hook this up in Spark Datasource
title: Enable ORC Writer for Spark

body: Should we add a code style check by maven-checkstyle-plugin? We can do it one by one for all sub modules.
title: Code style check for better code quality

body:
I think an Iceberg unstructured module would be great to have.  This is useful for datasets which do not have proper schema evolution rules [e.g csv] or are completely binary e.g ML models, but still can use Iceberg feature sets like snapshot isolation and partitioning.
This, of-course cannot be supported by any compute engine, this would be more of a standalone API like Iceberg generics module.
I'm unsure, we need  data reading capabilities. As a first version I'd be happy if we only support scan for the read side which can return the files as an Iterable, on the write side we can possibly support appending files to the table.
What do people think, should we build something like this?
title: [Proposal] An iceberg-unstructured module
Does iceberg support copy on write or merge on read?

title: HadoopTableOperations.commit is not an atomic operation

title: [InputFormat Followup] InputFiles should be created using FileIO and Encryption manager

title: [InputFormat Followup] Add residual evaluation for Iceberg generics

body:
Current implementation uses Avro as the intermediate fomat, as:
Input as Java Map, serialized to Avro IndexRecord (as the intermediate format), then call Parquet.write(Iceberg API) to write into Parquet file.

We need to remove that dependency and use Iceberg generic record/built-in types (maps with non-string keys, decimals, date/time types...) as the input (addressed)

Remove AvroSerializer and its implementations (renamed to RecordSerializer as we need a serializer here to transform input format to Iceberg Record))
Remove AvroUtils (addressed)
Remove the setting on serializer in IcebergSinkAppender (Kept as we need a serializer here)

Add the translation to/from Flink native formats (like we did for InternalRow for Spark) (will be addressed later)

FileWriter#write() could accept convention type in addition to Iceberg generic record. See this comment. (will be addressed later, currently, the code only supports Iceberg Record as input )
title: Use Iceberg generic record to replace Avro IndexedRecord and add a translation to/from data type in Flink

title: Remove Spectator

body:
We see few tasks failures for large tables because of s3 eventual consistency as getStatus us called immediately after creating file.
after checking s3 , file does exists. we have observed this issue in non-spark client as well.
one possible solution here is to use writer.length to get file size instead of calling getStatus
workaround (https://github.com/apache/incubator-iceberg/blob/master/spark/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/spark/source/Writer.java#L443)
//replace
.withEncryptedOutputFile(currentFile)
//with
.withEncryptionKeyMetadata(currentFile.keyMetadata())
.withPath(currentFile.encryptingOutputFile().location())
.withFileSizeInBytes(currentAppender.length())
